To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) human activities are responsible for a lasting open vegetation in the study area, (2) Holocene relative sea level rise has affected the coastal wetland since the beginning of the Holocene and (3) the Greco pond is an excellent example of a small island ecosystem where climate and human impact are both responsible for environmental changes.
the human impact was the leading factor in vegetation and beetle assemblage change in a small island.
human activities and climate were both responsible for the Holocene environmental changes in a small Mediterranean Island.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of human-climate-environments interactions in a small island in the Mediterranean Sea.
human-environment interactions in the Holocene and the role of human impact on biodiversity.
the reconstruction of the vegetation history of Cavallo Island, Corsica.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
human-climate-environments interactions are complex and that the effects of human activities on the environment are difficult to separate from those of climatic factors.
the Holocene history of the Greco pond was mainly influenced by the interplay of climate, human impact and sea-level changes.
the human impact is a major driving force of the Holocene vegetation and terrestrial beetle evolution on this Mediterranean small island.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
climate and human activities are both important drivers of Holocene environmental changes, but human impacts could be more influential than climate in a small island ecosystem.
the Holocene history of Cavallo Island is characterized by the alternation of human-induced open vegetation and coastal wetland development in response to the sea-level rise.
human activities have played a major role in vegetation and insect assemblage changes, while climate change has played a secondary role in the Greco Island.
The main takeaway from our work is that
small islands are very vulnerable to climate and sea-level change as well as to human activities, which could lead to a rapid and irreversible loss of biodiversity.
the Holocene relative rise sea level had a strong influence on the coastal wetlands of Corsica.
small islands are highly sensitive to environmental changes, which are often amplified by human impacts.
